faq.a: A government-backed mortgage for eligible rural properties with income limits, often allowing zero down payment.
An upfront fee (commonly financed) plus a small annual fee that replaces traditional mortgage insurance.

faq.q: Can I finance the guarantee fee?
faq.a: Yes, many borrowers roll the upfront guarantee fee into the loan amount subject to program rules.

faq.q: Are there income and location limits?
faq.a: Yes. USDA loans require household income to be under limits, and the property must be in an eligible rural area.

faq.q: How does USDA differ from FHA?
faq.a: USDA allows zero down with guarantee/annual fees; FHA requires a down payment and uses upfront/annual MIP, not location-based eligibility.
